title: Localizing a desktop app
when: The desktop app must ship in several languages, including menus, dialogs, tray items and native message boxes, with the OS language as the default.
prompt:
Goal: All visible text, including native dialog titles and tray labels, comes from locale files, the OS language is picked first and the user can switch.
Steps:
1. Files resources/locales/en.json and pt-BR.json with nested keys: { "menu": { "file": "File" }, "dialog": { "unsaved": "Save changes to {name}?" } }.
2. Default language: the saved setting, else navigator.language matched to the closest file (pt-BR, then pt, then en).
3. t(key, vars) looks up the key, falls back to English, replaces {name} placeholders and reports missing keys once in the log.
4. Plurals with new Intl.PluralRules(lang).select(n) and keys like "items.one" and "items.other".
5. Dates and numbers with Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat; never build them by hand.
6. Native strings too: pass t() results to showMessageBox, showOpenDialog titles, filter names and setTray menu items; rebuild the tray after a language change.
7. For right to left languages set document.dir = "rtl" and use logical CSS (margin-inline-start).
8. A test checks every locale file has the same keys as en.json.
Quality bar:
- No hard coded English left in the UI or native dialogs.
- Layouts survive strings 40 percent longer.
Pitfalls:
- Joining sentence parts in code, which breaks word order.
- Forgetting to translate shortcut hints and file filter names.
Verify:
- [ ] Locale files parse and share keys.
- [ ] Dialog and tray text uses t().
- [ ] html lang matches the current language.
Output: resources/locales/*.json, i18n.js and a key parity test.

examples.input: traduzir meu app desktop para inglês e espanhol
examples.output: locales/*.json with nested keys, t() with fallback, PluralRules, translated dialogs and tray, key parity test
